findings.title: Client removal now calls setPermissionsEnabled, which throws in V2
findings.body: The ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2. That class's setPermissionsEnabled (ClientPermissionsV2.java around line 193) throws UnsupportedOperationException. Deleting any client in a realm with V2 enabled will therefore fail or leave the realm in an inconsistent state. The listener should skip the V2 path, or ClientPermissionsV2 should implement the call as a no-op or resource cleanup.

findings.title: Per-client resource shadows the all-clients grant
findings.body: hasPermission(client, scope) only evaluates the client's own resource when one exists (lines 214-222). The all-clients fallback runs only when no resource exists for that client. If an admin has a realm-wide 'all clients' VIEW permission and later creates a client-specific permission for another scope on the same client, a resource is created for that client. The all-clients VIEW grant is then no longer considered for that client, and the admin loses access they should still have. The fallback should be evaluated in addition to, not instead of, the per-client resource.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the all-clients resource is missing
findings.body: In the fallback branch, getResourceTypeResource(...) can return null (for example when the schema is not supported or the Clients resource has not been created). The next line then calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) with a null resource, which causes an NPE on every client permission check instead of returning false. A null check is needed.

findings.title: requireView() javadoc describes a boolean return instead of a throw
findings.body: The javadoc for requireView() says 'Returns true if canView() returns true', but the method is void and should throw ForbiddenException when canView() returns false. The same wrong wording appears for requireViewClientScopes(), and the requireList/requireListClientScopes docs are similarly inconsistent with their methods.
